description: Rajas con Crema is a beloved Mexican vegetarian dish featuring tender strips of roasted poblano peppers bathed in a rich, creamy sauce. This comforting recipe combines the mild heat of poblanos with the savory notes of onion and garlic, all brought together by the lusciousness of Mexican crema or sour cream. It's a versatile dish that can be enjoyed as a hearty side, a flavorful taco filling, or a delicious main course.

ingredients.notes: roasted, peeled, seeded, and cut into strips

instructions.title: Roast the Poblano Peppers
instructions.text: Preheat your broiler or heat a comal or heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Place the poblano peppers directly over the flame, under the broiler, or on the hot surface, turning frequently until the skins are completely charred and blistered on all sides. This should take about 10-15 minutes. Transfer the charred peppers to a bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel. Let them steam for 10-15 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Rajas
instructions.text: Once the peppers have cooled enough to handle, peel off the charred skin. Make a slit down one side of each pepper, remove the seeds and veins, and discard them. Slice the cleaned poblano peppers into thin strips, known as rajas. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large skillet or non-stick pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced white onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Combine Peppers and Corn
instructions.text: Add the prepared poblano rajas and corn kernels to the skillet with the sautéed onion and garlic. Stir well to combine and cook for 3-5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the corn to heat through.

instructions.title: Prepare the Cream Sauce
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together the Mexican crema or sour cream, whole milk, and chicken or vegetable bouillon powder until smooth. Ensure there are no lumps from the bouillon.

instructions.title: Simmer to Perfection
instructions.text: Pour the cream mixture over the vegetables in the skillet. Stir gently to incorporate everything. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly and the flavors have fully combined. Season with salt to taste.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Remove from heat and let it rest for a minute. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro, if desired. Serve Rajas con Crema hot as a side dish, a filling for tacos or quesadillas, or alongside rice and beans.

tips: For perfectly roasted poblanos, ensure the skin is fully charred before steaming. This makes peeling much easier and enhances the smoky flavor of the rajas.
If you cant find Mexican crema, full-fat sour cream works as a great substitute. For an extra rich flavor, a touch of cream cheese can be melted into the sauce.
Rajas con Crema is incredibly versatile. Serve it as a side dish, a filling for soft tacos or quesadillas, or as a topping for sopes or tostadas. It also pairs wonderfully with grilled meats.
article:
Discover a culinary gem that’s both comforting and vibrant: Rajas con Crema. This traditional Mexican vegetarian dish, literally meaning "strips with cream," transforms humble poblano peppers into a rich, smoky, and incredibly satisfying roasted pepper cream. Perfect for a weeknight meal or a festive gathering, Rajas con Crema offers a taste of authentic Mexican cuisine that’s naturally vegetarian and bursting with flavor. If you're looking for a versatile dish that can be a main course, a side, or a filling, you've found your next favorite recipe. Let's delve into everything you need to know about preparing this delightful dish.

## What is Rajas con Crema?

Rajas con Crema is a beloved Mexican staple, celebrated for its creamy texture and the distinct smoky-sweet flavor of roasted poblano peppers. The "rajas" refer to the strips of roasted and peeled poblano peppers, which are the star of the show. These peppers, known for their mild heat and earthy notes, are charred until tender, then peeled to remove their tough outer skin, revealing their succulent flesh. Once prepared, the rajas are typically sautéed with onions and garlic, then simmered in a luscious cream sauce, often enhanced with a touch of milk, corn, and sometimes a hint of cheese.

This dish is a testament to the beauty of simple ingredients transformed through traditional techniques. It’s naturally vegetarian, making it an excellent choice for meatless Mondays or for those following a plant-based diet. The depth of flavor comes from the roasting process, which brings out the poblanos' inherent sweetness and introduces a delightful smokiness that pairs perfectly with the rich, dairy-based sauce. Rajas con Crema is incredibly versatile, adaptable to various meals and preferences, and always promises a hearty and flavorful experience.

## Ingredients for Rajas con Crema

Creating authentic Rajas con Crema requires a few key ingredients, most of which are readily available. The quality of your ingredients will significantly impact the final flavor profile.

*   **Poblano Peppers:** These are non-negotiable! You'll need about 4-6 large poblano peppers. They are mild to medium in heat, with a distinct earthy flavor that becomes smoky and sweeter when roasted.
*   **White Onion:** One medium onion, thinly sliced, provides a foundational aromatic sweetness.
*   **Garlic:** 3-4 cloves, minced, add essential pungent depth to the dish.
*   **Corn Kernels:** About 1 cup, fresh or frozen. Corn adds a touch of sweetness and textural contrast.
*   **Mexican Crema:** Approximately 1 cup. This is a crucial ingredient for the authentic creamy texture and tangy flavor. If unavailable, a mix of sour cream and heavy cream (or crème fraîche) can be a good substitute.
*   **Milk:** About 1/2 cup, whole milk or evaporated milk works best to thin the sauce to the right consistency without sacrificing richness.
*   **Oil:** 1-2 tablespoons of a neutral oil like canola or vegetable oil for sautéing.
*   **Salt and Pepper:** To taste, for seasoning.
*   **Optional Additions:** A pinch of dried oregano, a sprig of epazote (a traditional Mexican herb), or a handful of shredded Oaxaca cheese (or Monterey Jack) can elevate the flavor even further.

## How to Make Rajas con Crema: Step-by-Step Guide

Making Rajas con Crema is a rewarding process, largely due to the transformation of the poblano peppers. Follow these steps for a delicious outcome:

1.  **Roast the Poblano Peppers:** This is the most crucial step for flavor.
    *   **Method 1 (Grill/Gas Stove):** Place peppers directly over a medium-high flame on a gas burner or grill. Turn frequently with tongs until the skin is completely charred and blistered on all sides.
    *   **Method 2 (Oven Broiler):** Place peppers on a baking sheet and broil on high, turning every 5-7 minutes, until charred and blistered.
    *   Once charred, immediately transfer the hot peppers to a bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap or place them in a sealed plastic bag. Let them steam for 10-15 minutes. This makes peeling much easier.
2.  **Peel, Seed, and Slice the Peppers:** Once cool enough to handle, remove the charred skin. It should peel off easily. Cut each pepper lengthwise, remove the stem, seeds, and any white membranes. Slice the cleaned peppers into 1/4-inch wide strips (rajas).
3.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large skillet or Dutch oven, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the sliced white onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
4.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the poblano strips (rajas) and corn kernels to the skillet with the onion and garlic. Stir well and cook for 3-5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
5.  **Create the Cream Sauce:** In a separate small bowl, whisk together the Mexican crema and milk until smooth. Pour this mixture over the vegetables in the skillet. Stir gently to combine.
6.  **Season and Finish:** Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Season generously with salt and pepper to taste. If using, add optional herbs or cheese now. Let it simmer for 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has slightly thickened and all the flavors have melded beautifully.

## Tips for Perfect Rajas con Crema

Achieving the perfect Rajas con Crema involves a few considerations that can elevate your dish from good to outstanding.

*   **Don't Skip the Roasting:** The charring of the poblano peppers is essential. It not only makes them easier to peel but also infuses a deep, smoky flavor that defines the dish. Avoid boiling or steaming them instead, as this will result in a bland flavor.
*   **Proper Steaming:** Steaming the roasted peppers is key to easy peeling. Ensure they are well-sealed in a bowl or bag to trap the steam effectively.
*   **Adjust Heat Levels:** Poblano peppers are generally mild, but their heat can vary. If you prefer a spicier dish, you can leave some of the seeds and membranes in the peppers, or add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a finely diced serrano pepper to the sauté.
*   **Cream Consistency:** If your Rajas con Crema sauce becomes too thick, add a little more milk until it reaches your desired consistency. If it's too thin, let it simmer uncovered for a few more minutes to reduce.
*   **Freshness is Key:** While frozen corn works well, using fresh corn cut directly from the cob will add a superior sweetness and texture.
*   **Season as You Go:** Taste and adjust seasoning throughout the cooking process, especially after adding the cream.

## Serving Suggestions for Rajas con Crema

Rajas con Crema is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in numerous ways, making it a fantastic addition to your culinary repertoire.

*   **Tacos and Quesadillas:** This is perhaps the most popular way to enjoy Rajas con Crema. Spoon the creamy mixture into warm corn or flour tortillas for delicious vegetarian tacos, or use it as a filling for cheesy quesadillas.
*   **Side Dish:** It makes an excellent side dish for grilled meats, chicken, or fish, offering a creamy, flavorful contrast.
*   **Enchilada Filling:** Use it as a rich and flavorful vegetarian filling for enchiladas, topped with your favorite salsa and cheese.
*   **Eggs:** Serve it alongside scrambled eggs, in an omelet, or as a topping for huevos rancheros for a delightful breakfast or brunch.
*   **As a Dip:** Enjoy it warm with tortilla chips for a hearty and satisfying dip.
*   **Stuffed Bell Peppers:** Mix it with rice and stuff it into bell peppers for a comforting baked meal.
*   **With Rice or Beans:** A simple bowl of Rajas con Crema alongside Mexican rice or refried beans makes for a complete and satisfying meal.

## Rajas con Crema Variations & Substitutions

While the classic recipe for Rajas con Crema is perfect as is, there are many ways to customize it to your taste or dietary needs.

*   **Dairy-Free Version:** For a vegan or dairy-free option, substitute Mexican crema with a plant-based sour cream or cashew cream, and use a non-dairy milk (like almond or soy milk). Ensure your cheese substitute (if using) is also dairy-free.
*   **Add Cheese:** Stir in shredded Monterey Jack, Oaxaca, or even cream cheese (for extra richness) at the end until melted and smooth. This creates an even more decadent dish.
*   **Spice It Up:** For those who love heat, add a finely diced jalapeño or serrano pepper along with the poblano peppers, or a pinch of chipotle powder for smoky spice.
*   **Extra Vegetables:** Feel free to add other vegetables like diced zucchini, bell peppers (for color), or mushrooms for added texture and nutrients. Add them with the onions so they have time to cook through.
*   **Different Peppers:** While poblanos are traditional, you could experiment with other mild peppers like Anaheim or even a mix of bell peppers for a different flavor profile.
*   **Smoky Flavor Boost:** A tiny amount of liquid smoke (a drop or two) can enhance the smokiness if you didn't get enough char on your peppers.
*   **Herbs:** Fresh cilantro or a sprig of epazote (if you can find it) stirred in at the end can add a fresh, authentic Mexican touch.

Rajas con Crema is more than just a dish; it's an experience of robust flavors and comforting textures. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook, this Mexican vegetarian delight is surprisingly easy to make and guaranteed to impress. Give this roasted pepper cream a try, and you'll quickly understand why it's a staple in Mexican kitchens.
